name: Clubs
description:
Clubs

    enumi1

  1. Upland Mist — Hear horns but not edges; navigation by sound and instinct. `[WEATHER]` `[STEALTH]`

    The horns are calling a muster. Which clan? You will know when they arrive. The mist smells of wet wool and old iron. The horns sound in eights. The ninth note is a scream.

    Cairn vote: The mist is the breath of the cairns. Any failed roll here ticks Ancestral Grudge +1 (the dead are restless).

  2. Feud Rekindled — Cousin spits on guest-law; knives wake from sleep. `[SOCIAL]` `[COMBAT]`

    The spit lands at your feet. The insult is now yours to answer. The cousin's father was killed in a cattle raid thirty years ago. He has been waiting. He counts his grudges in eights. The ninth is you.

    Cairn vote: The nearest cairn is asked to judge. Roll a cairn vote (see table). On a Clean Success, the cairn votes for peace ((-1) segment on Feud timer). On a Miss, it votes for war (+2 segments).

  3. Bridge Dropped — Pursuers fall and the route with them; passage becomes peril. `[TRAP]` `[TRAVEL]`

    The bridge was cut from the far side. Someone expected you. The cut ropes smell of dwarf-made pitch—a signature of the Aeler outcasts. There were eight ropes. The ninth was cut first.

    Blood-price: If someone falls, their clan will demand a blood-price. Pay 2 Supply or start a Vendetta [6].

  4. Black-Rent Demand — “Privateering on land”; pay or be “escorted.” `[AUTHORITY]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The escort has a noose. Choose your words carefully. The man collecting is a Viterran factor with a royal warrant. The warrant is a forgery. No one will admit it. He demands eight silver. The ninth is your name.

    Guest-right cost: Pay 1 Supply or offer a hostage. Refusal starts The Viterran Yoke +1.

  5. Wergild Breach — Silver short by a head; tempers long by a spear's length. `[LAW]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The bereaved clan has a new widow. She is sharpening a blade. The missing silver was paid in lowland coin—debased, clipped, and worthless. The insult is not the shortfall; it is the contempt. She counts the coins in eights. The ninth is a blade.

    Cairn vote: The widow demands a cairn vote. Roll. On a 1–2, the dead vote for war—advance the related Feud timer by +3.

  6. Snow-Squall — Seals the notch; tents turn to coffins if you dally. `[WEATHER]` `[TRAVEL]`

    The snow is tinged gray—ash from the Pass. Someone burned an offering. The offering was a Viterran tax roll. The gods accepted. The snow falls in eights. The ninth flake is a memory.

    Guest-right cost: The only shelter is a cairn. Entering without an offering (1 Supply) angers the dead—start Ancestral Grudge +2.

  7. Dwarf Toll Hike — At the Steps; papers right, purses wrong; law costs coin. `[AUTHORITY]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The warden quotes a rate from a book that wasn't there yesterday. The book was written by an Aeler outcast who lost his sense of humor but not his reckoning. The rate is eight silver. The ninth is a story.

    Toll: Pay double (2 Supply) or offer a story about a broken promise. If you cannot, you are turned back—lose 1 segment of progress.

  8. Cattle Scatter — Bells ringing downslope; the cover story runs with the herd. `[STEALTH]` `[DISASTER]`

    The bells are yours. The herd is not. The real owner is a clan chief with a long memory and three sons with sharp swords. The bells ring in eights. The ninth is a war-cry.

    Blood-price: The chief demands 3 cows (1 Supply) as a fine. If you cannot pay, start a Cattle Raid Feud [6].

  9. False Alarm — Watch-fire beacons ridge to ridge; levies seize the road. `[WATCH]` `[AUTHORITY]`

    The fire was lit by a child. Or a spy. The levy doesn't care. The spy is a Viterran agent. The child is his nephew. The beacons burn in eights. The ninth is a lie.

    Cairn vote: The levy will not listen to reason. Roll a cairn vote to see if the dead intervene. On a 5–6, the mist swallows the levy—they disperse.

    J
    Bride-Theft — A wedding becomes a war-party; you are caught between both. `[SOCIAL]` `[COMBAT]`

    The bride's veil is on the ground. The groom's own kin drew first blood. The bride was promised to a neighboring clan. She chose her own groom. Now three clans want her head—and her hand. There are eight guests. The ninth is a ghost.

    Guest-right cost: Whoever you shelter, the other two clans will demand a wergild of 5 cows (2 Supply). Refusal starts a three-way feud.

    Q
    Royal Incursion — Neighbor's “lawful” arrests in the uplands; flags and chains. `[AUTHORITY]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The flags are Viterran. The chains are new. The prisoners are children. The crime is not paying a tax that was never law. The clans are calling the muster. The flags have eight stripes. The ninth is blood.

    Cairn vote: The cairns vote on whether to resist. Roll. On 1–2, the dead advise patience—the clans hesitate. On 5–6, they vote for war—advance The Viterran Yoke +2.

    K
    Clan Muster — Horns call men from steadings to spears; all traffic stops. `[WATCH]` `[COMBAT]`

    The muster stone is black with old blood. The new blood will be red. The last muster was forty years ago, to drive out a Viterran garrison. The garrison's bones are under the sheepwalk. The horns sound eight times. The ninth is silence.

    Blood-price: To pass through the muster, you must pay a blood-price to the clan's cairn—1 Supply or a hostage. Refusal means you are conscripted into the war.

    A
    Hill-Fall — Rain liquefies a slope; trail, proof, and bodies slide together. `[WEATHER]` `[DEATH]`

    The mud is warm. Something underneath is still breathing. The slide exposed a mass grave—clan warriors who fell in a forgotten feud. Their ghosts are counting the blood-price still outstanding. They count in eights. The ninth is you.

    Cairn vote: The ghosts demand payment. Pay 3 Supply (wergild for the dead) or roll a cairn vote. On 1–2, the ghosts attack—treat as a Cap 3 adversary.
